title: Materials to Take Us Beyond Concrete
titleArabic: مواد تأخذنا إلى ما وراء الخرسانة
story:
Concrete is the second most used substance in the global economy, after water – and one of the world's biggest single sources of greenhouse gas emissions. The chemical process by which cement, the key ingredient of concrete, is created results in large quantities of carbon dioxide. The UN estimates that there will be 9.8 billion people living on the planet by mid-century. They will need somewhere to live. If concrete is the only answer to the construction of new cities, then carbon emissions will soar, aggravating global warming. And so scientists have started innovating with other materials, in a scramble for alternatives to a universal commodity that has underpinned our modern life for many years.

The problem with replacing concrete is that it is so very good at what it does. The ingredients are relatively cheap and found in abundance. Concrete is mouldable and pourable, but quickly sets hard. Steel can be used to reinforce concrete, making it far stronger.

A possible alternative is wood. Recent years have seen tall buildings constructed almost entirely from timber in Vancouver, Vienna and Brumunddal in Norway. Cross-laminated timber is engineered wood where layers are glued together crosswise.

Fly ash and slag from iron ore are other alternatives. Fly ash can make up 15-30% of cement. However, Anna Surgenor notes that transportation costs may reduce environmental benefits.
translation: الخرسانة هي ثاني أكثر مادة استخداماً في الاقتصاد العالمي بعد الماء، وأحد أكبر مصادر غازات الاحتباس الحراري. العملية الكيميائية لإنتاج الأسمنت، المكون الرئيسي للخرسانة، ينتج عنها كميات كبيرة من ثاني أكسيد الكربون. تقديرات الأمم المتحدة تشير إلى 9.8 مليار نسمة بحلول منتصف القرن. سيحتاجون لمكان للعيش. إذا كانت الخرسانة هي الإجابة الوحيدة، فسترتفع الانبعاثات بشكل كبير.

topicNotes.en: 🏗️ The Concrete Dilemma: Concrete builds our cities but produces massive CO2 emissions. Scientists race to find alternatives: wood (tall timber buildings), cross-laminated timber, fly ash, and slag. But concrete is cheap, abundant, and amazing at what it does - making it hard to replace.

title: The Steam Car - The Doble Brothers' Story
story:
When primitive automobiles first appeared in the 1800s, their engines were based on steam power. But these early cars inherited steam's weaknesses: boilers had to be lit by hand, required 20 minutes to build pressure, and water reservoirs only lasted 30 miles.

But the glory days were few. The internal combustion engine appeared, offering ability to drive moments after starting. In 1912, General Motors introduced the electric starter, and steam power was gradually phased out.

Even as the market declined, four brothers made one last effort. Between 1906-1909, while still in high school, Abner Doble and his brothers built their first steam car in their parents' basement. The Model B (1914) could accelerate 0-60 in 15 seconds.

In 1916, the Model C added key-based ignition. 5,390 deposits were received. But the Model C had serious glitches.

The Model E (1924) was the final attempt. It started in 40 seconds even after freezing overnight, reached 100+ mph, with negligible emissions. But at $18,000, only 50 were ever made. The company folded in 1931.

Ironically, those surviving Model Es still run today, some with 500,000+ miles.
translation:
عندما ظهرت السيارات الأولى في 1800s، كانت محركاتها تعمل بالبخار. لكنها ورثت ضعف البخار: الغلايات تحتاج إشعالاً يدوياً، و20 دقيقة لبناء الضغط، والماء يكفي 30 ميلاً.

لكن أيام البخار انتهت. ظهر محرك الاحتراق الداخلي. في 1912، قدمت جنرال موتورز بادئ كهربائي، وتدريجياً تم التخلي عن البخار.

بين 1906-1909، وهم في الثانوية، بنى أبنر دوبل وإخوته أول سيارة بخار في قبو والديهم. موديل B (1914) تسارع من 0-60 في 15 ثانية.

في 1916، أضاف موديل C إشعالاً بالمفتاح. استُلم 5390 عربوناً.

موديل E (1924) كانت المحاولة الأخيرة. تبدأ في 40 ثانية بعد التجمد، 100+ ميل/ساعة، انبعاثات ضئيلة. لكن بـ18000 دولار، صُنعت 50 فقط. انهارت الشركة 1931.

title: How to Make Wise Decisions
story:
For centuries, wisdom was considered rare—a gift for philosophers and elders. But modern research reveals wisdom isn't a personality trait you either have or don't. It's a skill that depends on context.

Professor Igor Grossmann discovered that wisdom varies dramatically based on situations. Your ability to reason wisely changes depending on your experiences, the culture you're in, and the specific situation you face.

The four keys to wise reasoning are:
1. Intellectual humility - knowing you don't know everything
2. Perspective-taking - seeing beyond your own viewpoint
3. Change recognition - understanding relationships evolve
4. Compromise - integrating different beliefs

The 'fly on the wall' technique: Pretend you're an outsider watching your own situation. Research proves this works. Students imagining careers as distant observers made wiser choices. Couples viewing conflicts through others' eyes found better compromises.

Wisdom has almost no connection to IQ or personality. A person can be wise in one situation and foolish in another. The situation matters more than the person.

Next time you face a difficult decision, step back and ask: 'What would I advise a friend in this situation?' This simple shift unlocks hidden wisdom.
translation:
لقرون، اعتُبرت الحكمة نادرة—هبة للفلاسفة وكبار السن. لكن البحث الحديث يكشف أن الحكمة ليست سمة شخصية. إنها مهارة تعتمد على السياق.

اكتشف البروفيسور إيغور غروسمان أن الحكمة تختلف بناءً على المواقف. قدرتك على التفكير بحكمة تتغير حسب تجاربك، ثقافتك، والموقف المحدد.

المفاتيح الأربعة للتفكير الحكيم:
1. التواضع الفكري
2. أخذ منظور الآخر
3. التعرف على التغيير
4. التوصل لحل وسط

تقنية 'الذبابة على الحائط': تظاهر أنك خارجي يراقب موقفك. البحث يثبت أن هذا يعمل.

الحكمة ليس لها علاقة تقريباً بمعدل الذكاء أو الشخصية. الموقف يهم أكثر من الشخص.

topicNotes.en: 🧠 The Science of Wisdom: Wisdom isn't a rare gift—it's a skill anyone can develop! Four keys: intellectual humility, perspective-taking, change recognition, and compromise. The 'fly on the wall' technique: pretend advising a friend = wiser decisions. Wisdom barely relates to IQ!
